label: related
point: Held the upward departure for dangerousness was legal error, noting in a footnote that 3742(e)'s due-deference standard does not bar reversal of an erroneous legal conclusion.
change: The PROTECT Act rewrote 3742(e)(3) to list departure grounds and required de novo review of departure determinations.
why: The new de novo standard concerns the same review provision but would only strengthen the reversal Moses reached; it does not change the decision's point.

label: related
point: Affirmed a sex-trafficking restitution award under 1593, applying the 2259(b)(3) definition of 'full amount of the victim's losses' with a proximate-cause requirement.
change: The 2018 Act added a special restitution rule for child-pornography trafficking (relative-role amount, $3,000 floor) and moved the losses definition out of 2259(b).
why: The change targets child-pornography trafficking cases after Paroline, not sex-trafficking restitution under 1593, so the decision's result stands.

label: unrelated
point: Cited the EAJA net-worth limits in 2412(d) in passing to hold that 7491(a) burden-shifting did not apply to the partnerships.
change: Replaced references to the Contract Disputes Act of 1978 with 'chapter 71 of title 41' (positive-law codification).
why: A pure cross-reference change unrelated to the net-worth point the decision used.

label: codifies
point: Held the CDA's 'indecent' transmission provision of 223(a)(1)(B) (and the 223(d) patently offensive provision) unconstitutional under the First Amendment.
change: The PROTECT Act struck 'indecent' (and 'lewd, lascivious, filthy') from 223(a)(1), substituting 'obscene or child pornography'.
why: Congress removed the very words Reno invalidated, conforming the statute to the decision; the report cites Reno, though in discussing another provision.

label: unrelated
point: Mentioned 4221(a) only in describing Clintwood Elkhorn's coal-export tax facts while holding the arbitrage-rebate takings claim barred for failure to exhaust refund remedies.
change: Added a sentence that certain 4221(a) exemptions do not apply to the new medical device tax under 4191.
why: The change has nothing to do with the decision's exhaustion holding.

label: codifies
point: Held the CPPA's 'appears to be' a minor definition in 2256(8)(B) unconstitutionally vague and overbroad and dismissed the possession charge.
change: Replaced 'is, or appears to be, of a minor' with digital/computer images 'indistinguishable from' a minor, and struck the 'conveys the impression' clause.
why: After Free Speech Coalition, Congress dropped the 'appears to be' language this decision struck down, moving the statute toward its holding; the report names the First Circuit's reversal of this decision only in listing circuits that had upheld the CPPA.

label: related
point: Held the Veterans Court could not invoke 7261(b) harmless error to affirm on a well-grounded-claim ground the Board had not relied on and the claimant had no notice of.
change: Required the Veterans Court to review the whole record and take due account of the Secretary's application of the benefit-of-the-doubt rule, alongside prejudicial error.
why: Same review provision, but the amendment does not change the rule that harmless error cannot rest on an unnoticed well-grounded finding.

label: related
point: Held 4712(a) protects employees of all federal grantees (including the housing authority), but affirmed because the employee's belief of gross mismanagement was not reasonable.
change: Re-punctuated the list of covered employers and added personal services contractors to the management officials who may receive disclosures.
why: The change keeps grantee coverage intact and does not affect the reasonable-belief ground of decision.

label: unrelated
point: Cited section 504's nondiscrimination rule while affirming closure of a vocational rehabilitation case for refusal to participate in evaluation.
change: Changed the cross-reference for the disability definition from section 706(8) to 705(20).
why: A renumbered cross-reference only.

label: related
point: Held the PSLRA's 78u-4(b)(2) pleading standard did not eliminate recklessness as a basis for scienter and the complaint met it.
change: SLUSA added 78u-4(b)(3)(D) allowing courts to stay state-court discovery to prevent circumvention of the PSLRA discovery stay.
why: The SLUSA report lists the decision among cases on the PSLRA pleading standard, but the law changed only the discovery-stay paragraph, not the pleading or scienter rule.

label: related
point: Affirmed denial of suppression, finding probable cause for the warrant; the 2256(2)(A)(v) lascivious-exhibition definition figured in a footnote and the dissent.
change: Added 'anus' to the lascivious-exhibition category of sexually explicit conduct.
why: Same definition, but adding a body part does not affect the probable-cause analysis the court performed.

label: unrelated
point: The en banc dissent argued ERISA's anti-alienation and QDRO provisions (1056(d)) preempt Louisiana community-property claims by a predeceasing spouse's heirs.
change: Added 1056(d)(4)-(5) allowing pension offsets for amounts owed the plan from fiduciary-breach judgments or settlements, with spousal protections.
why: The offset exception is unrelated to community-property preemption; the report's mention of the Supreme Court's Boggs decision concerns a separate estate-tax provision and disclaims any change to its result.

label: override_implicit
point: Held that 2401e(a)(1)(C)'s net-income test requires comparing the producer's most recent year with the immediately preceding year, rejecting the Department's non-consecutive-year comparison, and remanded.
change: ARRA rewrote 2401e(a)(1), eliminating the net farm income comparison and substituting production, price, and county-price decline tests tied to the petition marketing year.
why: The net-income requirement the decision construed was removed, so its reasoning no longer applies; nothing shows Congress was responding to this case rather than overhauling the program.

label: unrelated
point: Quoted the TILA definition of 'credit' in deciding when an extension of credit occurs for California's setoff statute.
change: Dodd-Frank redesignated the TILA definitions so subsection (e) now defines 'person'; the 'credit' definition moved unchanged.
why: Renumbering only.

label: related
point: Denied a preliminary injunction on the dilution claim because linking a vulgar domain to ford.com was not a 'commercial use' of the mark.
change: The TDRA rewrote 1125(c) to a likelihood-of-dilution standard by blurring or tarnishment, dropping 'commercial use in commerce' from the cause of action but keeping an exclusion for noncommercial use.
why: Same provision and subject, but noncommercial use remains excluded, so the result on the decision's point would not change.

label: unrelated
point: Upheld the CPPA's definition of child pornography (2252A/2256(8)) against First Amendment challenge.
change: The PROTECT Act raised penalties in 2252(b) (mandatory minimums, higher maximums) and added predicate offenses.
why: The 2252 penalty changes have nothing to do with the constitutional holding; the report names Mento only in listing circuits that upheld the CPPA before Free Speech Coalition.

label: unrelated
point: Held that a plan amendment expanding disqualifying post-retirement employment violated ERISA's anti-cutback rule in 1054(g).
change: Changed the cross-reference in 1054(g)(1) from section 1082(c)(8) to 1082(d)(2).
why: Cross-reference update only.

label: unrelated
point: Held a top-of-range sentence unreviewable and the district court's reasons sufficient under 3553(c)(1).
change: Required departure reasons under 3553(c)(2) to be stated in the written judgment and sent to the Sentencing Commission.
why: The amendment concerns (c)(2) departures and record transmission, not the (c)(1) within-range statement the decision applied; the report names a different Sims (D.N.M.).

label: unrelated
point: Applied the 282 presumption of validity in reversing the Federal Circuit's rigid TSM obviousness test under section 103.
change: The AIA barred failure to disclose best mode as a ground for invalidity under 282(b)(3).
why: The best-mode change has nothing to do with obviousness; the report names KSR only in listing Supreme Court reversals of the Federal Circuit.

label: related
point: Held the district court could not delegate to the probation officer the amount and schedule of restitution, which 3556/3663 entrust to the court.
change: The MVRA made restitution mandatory under 3663A for certain offenses and applied 3664 procedures to all restitution orders.
why: Same restitution provision, but the mandatory-restitution change does not alter the non-delegation point.

label: unrelated
point: Cited 3553 factors as part of the revocation framework while holding a nolo contendere conviction may prove a supervised-release violation.
change: Changed where departure reasons must be stated to the statement of reasons form under 28 U.S.C. 994(w)(1)(B).
why: Unrelated technical change to 3553(c)(2).

label: unrelated
point: Held a challenge to DoD in-sourcing under 2463 procedures was a bid protest within the Court of Federal Claims' exclusive Tucker Act jurisdiction.
change: Added critical and acquisition-workforce functions to the special-consideration list, cost-comparison rules for conversions, and contractor notification.
why: The substantive in-sourcing changes do not touch the jurisdictional holding; the report names a different Rothe case (545 F.3d 1023, price-preference challenge).

label: unrelated
point: Held petitioner ineligible for cancellation because he showed no qualifying relative under 1229b(b)(1)(D) and dismissed other claims for lack of jurisdiction.
change: Added 1229b(b)(6) authorizing parole of relatives of trafficking victims granted continued presence.
why: The new parole paragraph has nothing to do with the qualifying-relative requirement.
